title: MDAAI
description: MDAAI is a protocol for governing AI-assisted development. Choose and configure a template to apply its rules for authority, scope, evidence and review.

sections.title: Apply the protocol with a template
sections.text: To apply the protocol, choose and configure a template. A template supplies the concrete governance files; agents, coding harnesses and execution tools are separate layers. The protocol defines a method for authority, scope, evidence, history and review—not an executor. The templates documented here put that method in Markdown and JSON files alongside your project.

sections.title: Continuity without duplicate state
sections.text: A new session should be able to find the authorized task, its acceptance criteria, current evidence and next action without reconstructing a conversation. In MDAAI 2.0, Project Elaboration owns scope and sequence; TASKS.json owns task state. Keeping each fact with one owner avoids conflicting status checkboxes, parallel registries and repeated work.

sections.title: What adoption adds—and does not add
sections.text: The MDAAI 2.0 template family supplies a root AGENTS.md, five governance documents, project-owned Project Elaboration and a fresh TASKS.json. For any agent system, point its entry instructions to the nearest AGENTS.md. Applicable parent and scoped governance files are cumulative. Adoption is an explicitly authorized, project-by-project merge and migration, not a universal installer. The source package’s research code, dashboards, studies and existing task history are not copied into every adopted repository.

sections.title: Two initial template families
sections.text: The first-generation template uses an elaborated project plan, Work Orders, a work-order registry, corrective records and architecture decisions. MDAAI 2.0 concentrates routine work in one task registry and adds separate records only when they carry necessary context. A migration reconciles contradictory instructions and preserves completed history; it does not layer another active template over unreconciled rules. These are concrete template families implementing MDAAI, not the whole protocol. Template versions and protocol identities are distinct.

sections.title: Protocol, templates and execution
sections.text: MDAAI defines the governance method. Versioned templates supply project files that apply it. Your selected agents, coding harnesses and execution tools read those files and perform authorized work. Permissions, tests and runtime checks belong to those separate execution layers; choosing a template does not install or activate them.

sections.title: Instructions are not automatic enforcement
sections.text: Markdown instructions guide agent behavior. Structural validators can check fields, references and consistency; they cannot establish that a claim is true, grant authorization or prove a product works. Actual tests and relevant runtime observation support acceptance. Automated revision/publication software is a separate implementation with separate approvals—not a consequence of reading AGENTS.md.

templateCycle.title: A stable protocol. Templates that evolve.
templateCycle.text: The protocol governs how work is authorized, reviewed and evidenced. A template gives that method a concrete home in project files. Improve those files through reviewed work; adopt a new version explicitly. The protocol can itself be revised through its own authorized process.
templateCycle.note: Review may be manual or agent-assisted. Publication does not activate a template or update your project.

title: MDAAI: A Protocol for Governing AI-Assisted Development
description: A documentary design account of authority, scope, evidence, history and review in AI-assisted development.

sections.title: Download the paper
sections.text: Preprint / documentary design paper. Published on the author’s website; no journal publication or peer-review claim is made.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.text: When an AI-assisted coding task stops between an edit and its verification, the next participant needs more than the patch. They need to know what was authorized, what remains unresolved, and which observations support the recorded result. MDAAI governs AI-assisted development through rules for authority, scope, evidence, history, and review. This paper uses interruption as a lens on that broader purpose, following a hypothetical date-parser repair through two template representations: a work-order document with a synchronized index, and a task registry with conditional supporting records. The comparison distinguishes internal record consistency from reconciliation with the current implementation, and prescribed narrative records from judgment about when a separate explanation is needed. The contribution is a documentary design account, not a measurement of improved task performance. Testing must establish whether recording and reconciliation prevent enough recovery and acceptance errors to justify their cost.

sections.title: Author and affiliation
sections.text: Eris Margeta Kurdali · TEJL — Tvornica Elektroničkih Jedinica i Logike, Croatia · eris.margeta@gmail.com · TEJL.com · TEJL.hr

title: Repository structure
description: The MDAAI 2.0 template family’s governance files: entry instructions, authority, scope, task state and evidence ownership.

sections.title: Files and information owners
sections.text: This map describes the MDAAI 2.0 template family, not a universal file inventory required by the protocol. Required means required by this template contract. At adoption, merge the governance instructions and author the two management files for the target project. The map below uses exact core paths. Conditional pattern rows describe record categories, not files an installer creates. Each core file has an explanatory section linked below.

sections.title: AGENTS.md
sections.text: Start here. Its operating contract tells the agent to read the assigned task and only named relevant references, preserves higher-level and nearest-repository constraints, and links authority, engineering, evidence, reasoning and records. It is not the place for a second task list.

sections.title: Agent entry instructions
sections.text: For any agent system, point its entry instructions to the nearest AGENTS.md. Applicable parent and scoped governance files are cumulative.

sections.title: AUTHORITY.md
sections.text: Owns the boundary between bounded implementation and effects needing action-time authorization. It covers data classification, credentials, Git and protected work. Read before the affected action. Writing an active task or plan never expands permission.

sections.title: ENGINEERING.md
sections.text: Owns implementation and defect-repair rules. Domain invariants stay with their domain owner. Architecture changes get a compact ADR when warranted. Defects follow investigation → faithful regression → adjacent-test audit → red → root fix → affected green; expected red tests are not new corrective work orders.

sections.title: EVIDENCE.md
sections.text: Owns what level of proof an acceptance claim needs. Documentation checks, unit tests, ordinary startup, real-browser observation and deployed-state verification are distinct. The task stores references and results; the evidence file does not repeat task status.

sections.title: REASONING.md
sections.text: Owns economical context gathering and coordination. Read relevant records first, expand only for a concrete uncertainty, give each mutable file one writer, and leave shared integration/status to the coordinator. It does not prescribe a personal model launcher or local agent configuration.

sections.title: RECORDS.md
sections.text: Owns task/record semantics and recovery rules. It links the management registry and defines lifecycle states separately from scheduling disposition. Active records can evolve; coherent terminal results are preserved and corrected through linked supersession.

sections.title: PROJECT-ELABORATION.md
sections.text: Owns the project’s authorized scope and delivery order. The adopting project writes its own content. It links TASKS.json for live status and evidence, rather than copying progress checkboxes. Change it when project scope or sequencing changes—not for every state transition.

sections.title: TASKS.json
sections.text: Owns current tasks and their audit history. A task has a stable project-prefixed ID, owner, scopeRef, acceptance criteria, state, disposition, evidence, blocker, next action, dependencies and history. The owner/coordinator updates active work here. Start with a fresh target-specific registry; do not copy the source package’s tasks.

sections.title: Conditional decisions
sections.text: ENGINEERING.md requires a compact ADR for architecture changes. Preserve accepted decisions and supersede them when warranted. The portable 2.0 adoption guide does not mandate a fixed ADR filename or an ADR template; use the target’s decision convention and link the actual file.

sections.title: Conditional context records
sections.text: RECORDS.md permits a short durable record when a material decision, defect cause, review, handoff or external effect needs context beyond the task/evidence. Include ID/date, owner, scope, decision/mechanism, result/limits, next action and supersession link as applicable. No routine WO, CWO or checkpoint is required. PROJECT-INTERNAL/RECORDS/ is a source-package location, not a mandatory adoption artifact.

sections.title: Evidence artifacts
sections.text: TASKS.json evidence entries reference project-local artifacts when possible. Their exact paths and formats depend on the checks performed. Evidence identifies what was observed; a digest or log alone is not semantic proof. Generated runtime dependencies are not automatically disposable.

title: How files work together
description: How the MDAAI 2.0 template family connects instructions, project scope, task records and evidence without duplicating state.

sections.title: Startup reading order
sections.text: Read the applicable AGENTS.md and the assigned TASKS.json row first. Follow scopeRef to Project Elaboration or the actual scope owner; read linked evidence and only relevant governance references. Inspect the current working tree/runtime before resuming. Do not execute deferred tasks merely because they are visible. The source entry point names instructions → assigned task → relevant references; this diagram expands those actual relationships, not a new mandatory ceremony.

sections.title: Read, write and reference directions
sections.text: AGENTS.md supplies the operating contract; the rule documents constrain work. TASKS.json points to scope and evidence. Project Elaboration links back to the registry for status. The executor reads these inputs, changes only authorized product files, and writes actual evidence; the task owner/coordinator updates the canonical row. Architecture decisions and other durable records are conditional supporting references.

sections.title: Why not duplicate status?
sections.text: A project plan may say “implement request validation before UI integration,” while the registry says that validation is active and its next action is a boundary test. Those are different facts. Updating active state in both a Markdown checkbox list and JSON creates competing answers. Put scope/order in Project Elaboration, current progress in TASKS.json, actual observations in evidence, and architectural rationale in the decision record.

sections.title: What changes during ordinary work
sections.text: Usually the implementation, relevant tests/docs, evidence artifacts and one active task row change. Governance files do not need an edit for each feature. Project Elaboration changes only for scope/sequence changes. An ADR appears only for a relevant architecture decision; a separate durable record appears only for context the row and evidence cannot carry clearly.

sections.title: History and recovery
sections.text: Append a concise transition for lifecycle/disposition changes. Once a record has a coherent terminal result, preserve its meaning. A later discovered defect gets its own task with a link to the earlier result; material corrections use linked supersession. The registry can add that correction link without deleting the old transition. Resumption uses current nonterminal rows, linked evidence and live state—not an unbounded replay of old conversations.

title: Task lifecycle
description: An illustrative task in the MDAAI 2.0 template family, from authorized scope through verification, recorded evidence and later correction.

sections.title: 1. Establish the task and its scope
sections.text: The operator authorizes a read-only status endpoint. The executor reads AGENTS.md, the assigned APP-001 row, its scopeRef and applicable rule documents. Confirm that the endpoint is within project scope and that no external effect is being smuggled into the task. Read current working files before editing; preserve unrelated changes.

sections.title: 2. Keep one active task record
sections.text: This complete minimal registry uses fields checked by the source scripts/validate.py. APP is an illustrative project prefix. The scope file must actually exist. The ISO date and single active history entry satisfy that source validator; the task is not complete, has no invented evidence and names a useful next action.

sections.title: 3. Implement and collect evidence
sections.text: Write endpoint code and relevant tests/docs in the existing project layout. Check response shape and unsupported methods, then affected integration/runtime paths appropriate to the application. Save actual results at project-selected paths and update evidence/next in the active row. No routine Work Order or checkpoint is added. If this were a bug fix, capture a faithful pre-fix regression where safely possible before the root fix.

sections.title: 4. Add context only when necessary
sections.text: If the endpoint forces an architecture choice—such as a new service boundary—record alternatives, decision, migration/rollback and limits in the project’s compact ADR and link it. Otherwise no ADR is needed. A deployment or production write would need its applicable authorization and evidence; local implementation success does not authorize it.

sections.title: 5. Record a terminal result, not an invented one
sections.text: Only after actual evidence supports every acceptance criterion should the owner/coordinator set state to complete, disposition to current, blocker and next to null, attach criterion-indexed evidence, and append the complete transition. The fragment below is structural notation, not a completed sample: substitute a real local reference and observed result. Do not record success merely because the JSON validates.

sections.title: Blocked and deferred are different
sections.text: If APP-001 cannot proceed, blocked requires a concrete blocker and useful next action; resume blocked → active before completing. A separate unrelated defect may be recorded as active or proposed with deferred disposition, impact and next action, but it is not automatically authorized. A relevant defect still blocks the acceptance it invalidates.

rows: Evidence covers every criterion; next and blocker null; terminal disposition current.
Concise state/disposition transitions; preserve coherent terminal history.

sections.title: 6. Resume or correct later
sections.text: A new session reads APP-001 and its evidence, checks live state and continues only authorized nonterminal work. If the completed endpoint later proves defective, create a new task linked to APP-001 and retain the earlier evidence. Do not silently rewrite the old completed result into a different history.

title: First-generation template
description: The first-generation MDAAI template family uses Work Orders, corrective records, architecture decisions and checkpoints to govern project work.

sections.title: What the template puts in a repository
sections.text: Instantiation copies a repository template and customizes project-specific metadata and management content. The template includes governance, management, work-order and architecture scaffolding. Work Orders and later decisions are authored during work; they are not all pre-generated by instantiation. The template’s sync manifest separates inherited instructions from project-owned history so upstream synchronization does not overwrite local plans or work records.

sections.title: First-generation file map
sections.text: The following groups are present in the inspected canonical template. “Checked” names the template validator’s required-file checks; it does not imply every unchecked policy is optional. Root README.md, VERSION, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md are also baseline template files, not per-task records.

sections.title: A Work Order connects authorization to the change
sections.text: A task reference points from the order back to the operator request or Project Elaboration; Related ADR and Depends On link decisions and predecessor work. Reserve a number in WORK-ORDERS/registry.json and open the work-order-template.md record before implementation. Pending and active Work Orders may be updated with scope, files and actual verification; close only when acceptance evidence and actual expenditure are recorded. Closed WOs, corrective records and checkpoints remain immutable: later corrections use a linked corrective or superseding record. Register completion and WO links in Project Elaboration. The released template reconciles the prior editing-rule conflict; declarative rules and schemas do not themselves enforce permissions or prove evidence.

sections.title: CWO and ADR serve different purposes
sections.text: A CWO captures an error’s classification, root cause, correction, prevention and verification. An ADR captures the context, decision drivers, alternatives, chosen outcome and validation for an architecture decision. Neither is a substitute for the authorized project task. Completed work and accepted decisions retain historical meaning; later decisions supersede rather than silently erase accepted ADRs.

sections.title: Checkpoints certify milestones, not each edit
sections.text: CHECKPOINT-PROTOCOL.md requires a checkpoint at phase completion, a major version increment, finalized ADR implementation, a significant milestone or an operator request. Before creating it, synchronize relevant project knowledge, ensure WOs/CWOs are resolved and logged, run the required tests, update documentation and obtain human approval. The checkpoint gathers scope, deliverables, work orders, files, verification and next-phase context. It is immutable after creation; errors require a linked CWO, not an edit to the certificate.

sections.title: Source note
sections.text: MDAAI 1.0 is a template name; its independent release is 1.0.1. Its constitution internal revision is 1.8, with historical 1.7/header metadata retained as origin history. Neither number is the standalone MDAAI protocol version (1.0.0). The corrected public release permits pending/active work-record updates and protects closed history. Original upstream sources and their historical hashes remain unchanged; 43 historical source-link gaps are documented separately from verified canonical public payloads.

title: MDAAI 2.0 template
description: The MDAAI 2.0 template family uses a portable governance contract, one task registry and evidence-backed history. Adoption is project-specific.

sections.title: What gets added at adoption
sections.text: docs/ADOPTION.md defines a project-by-project pilot: inventory existing constraints/history and recovery state; reconcile conflicting first-generation rules; explicitly merge the root contract and five governance documents; author target-specific Elaboration and a fresh registry. A successful governance-file revision is not wholesale version adoption. No automatic installer or mass migration is implied. Record the selected authority in the pilot ADR. Adoption acceptance requires structural and targeted product checks, applicable ordinary startup/browser/device evidence, and a pilot exercising active-record editing, a deferred defect, a terminal result and resumption.

sections.title: Start with the target’s history, not the source’s
sections.text: The adoption guide specifies schemaVersion 1, a project-specific uppercase taskPrefix and an empty tasks array. Add target-owned task rows before claiming work is active. Do not copy M20 tasks, the source proposal analysis or its package-specific ADR as the target’s task history.

sections.title: What changes from the first generation
sections.text: The simplification is about where routine facts live, not removing all architecture or correction records. Reconcile root/nested instructions and older mandatory WO/checkpoint policies before activation. Preserve terminal legacy records unchanged; map active WO/CWO work to stable task rows or linked deferred entries.

sections.title: What does not belong in every adopted repository
sections.text: The source package’s README.md, VERSION, Justfile, proposal analysis, governance-v2 ADR, adoption documentation, laboratory code, dashboards, formal models and studies belong to that package. Its scripts/validate.py REQUIRED list includes package-delivery files; that is not the portable adoption inventory. Validator/tests are optional tools to adapt. Add real project commands only when they exist; merely copying tools does not test the target product.

sections.title: Mapping and rollback
sections.text: Active legacy WO/CWO records map to one canonical task row, with an extra linked record only for needed context. Completed/void records and checkpoints stay historical. Keep accepted ADRs; new decisions supersede them. For a failed pilot, preserve failure evidence and perform an authorized restoration of the pre-adoption instructions/status mapping. Governance rollback does not automatically undo product changes or external effects.

sections.title: Protocol and software are separate
sections.text: The inspected MDAAI 2.0 source package also contains research and governance-revision software. That software is separate from the MDAAI protocol and is not installed by adopting this template. Agents, coding harnesses and execution tools remain independently selected and configured. Structural checks do not prove that an agent follows the rules or that a product works.

title: Templates
description: Choose a template to apply the MDAAI protocol. Configure its governance files for your project; agents and execution tools are separate layers.

sections.title: Versions and export boundaries
sections.text: MDAAI protocol release 1.0.0 is independent of the named templates MDAAI 1.0 (release 1.0.1) and MDAAI 2.0 (release 2.0.1). Catalog 0.1.1, schema 1, imports immutable public package revisions through the same reviewed admission path as community templates: 91 and 18 verified literal payloads. The first template constitution internal revision is 1.8; historical document labels are origin metadata, not protocol releases. MDAAI 2.0 supplies six portable core files and project-owned Elaboration and TASKS.json scaffolds. Review and configure either package before adoption. Imported previews and downloads are read-only derivatives, not editable template authority.

sections.title: Review before adoption
sections.text: Both bundles are marked review-before-adoption and complete: false. All 105 listed files are exported; this status describes uninitialized downstream scaffolds, adoption review and known literal link gaps, not missing export files. First-generation references to PROJECT-DEVELOPMENT-ELABORATION.md and GUIDES/CHECKPOINT-PROTOCOL.md need reconciliation with the supplied owners. Review the export manifest, license scopes and known link-gap inventory. Back up the target, choose one active governance template configuration, reconcile existing rules, fill project identity and actual commands, then exercise a real task and resumption. No installer, automatic activation or guaranteed self-improvement is provided.

sections.title: Improve, version, then adopt
sections.text: Project experience can inform template improvements, manually or with agent assistance under the applicable protocol. Review the change and its evidence, publish a versioned template, then explicitly decide whether and how each project adopts it. A stable protocol governs this loop and may itself be revised through authorized review.
